summary: game.c rng_range() took a modulo of a full-range uint32_t RNG value, which CC compiles as signed idiv, so sign-bit-set values gave a negative index and an out-of-bounds moves[] read (garbage move name, absurd damage).
evidence: Found a real bug: `rng_range`'s modulo on a full-range `uint32_t` hits CC's known "signed-`idiv`-only" limitation

summary: Agent's `pkill -f 'qemu-system-i386...'` patterns matched the invoking bash command line itself, killing the shell (exit 144/1) so the rest of the command (QEMU launch, make) never ran, e.g. QEMU never started and later connects/monitor socket failed.

Serial driver/recording script waited for the boot banner, but a QEMU `server,nowait` serial socket discards guest output written before a client connects, so the banner never arrived and the script timed out.
evidence: fix the script to not depend on catching the boot banner (a `server,nowait` socket discards output written before a client connects)

summary: During the 5-minute recording the QEMU serial socket connection went quiet mid-battle although the guest stayed alive, so the play script timed out waiting for an end state; longer timeout did not help, reconnect-on-stall logic was needed.
evidence: I hit a QEMU serial-socket quirk (a connection occasionally went quiet mid-session even though the guest stayed alive and responsive) and added reconnect-on-stall logic

summary: Switching to mode 13h and drawing clobbered the text-mode font in VGA plane 2, and vga_set_text_mode only restored registers, so the shell showed garbage glyphs after returning to text mode.
evidence: drawing in mode 13h clobbers it - text mode "restores" registers-wise but shows garbage glyphs. I need to reload the font into plane 2.

summary: vga_select_font_plane used wrong register values for plane-2 access (SEQ[4] 0x07 with chain bit instead of 0x06, GC[6] 0x00/0x04/0x05 guesses), so the restored font did not land in plane 2.
evidence: my font-access values had bits wrong (an extra bit set in SEQ[4], and GC[6] pointing at the wrong addressing mode)

summary: vga_set_text_mode restored the font into plane 2 before loading text-mode CRTC/AC registers, but plane-2 writes only land correctly once the CRTC is in a text-like state, so after-restore plane contents were still wrong.
evidence: vga_debug_dump_font showed that plane-2 reads/writes at 0xA0000 only land correctly when the CRTC is already in a text-mode-like state
